title: CUSTOMER VEHICLE PROTECT-O-PLATE
summary: Protect-O-Plate (the stamped owner's warranty ID plate): what is stamped where on the plate (VIN, carburetor source, engine and rear axle codes, month built, transmission, power steering/brakes, radio, A/C, power windows) and how it is mounted. The stamped plate is stuck onto the adhesive-backed pocket inside the new-vehicle warranty folder; no fasteners.

parts.name: FOLDER-NEW VEH WARRANTY
parts.name_expanded: Folder – new vehicle warranty (owner's warranty booklet)

fastening.to: adhesive-backed portion of the warranty folder [2]
fastening.note: After stamping, plate [1] is pressed onto the adhesive-backed area inside folder [2] (shaded area in the folder view). Adhesive is part of the folder, not a separate material code.

notes: Stamp the plate with No. 35 size type; the stamped side must read normally (not mirrored).
Data longer than one character starts at the indicated location and continues to the right.
Plate is 33 columns long and 9 rows deep when No. 28 size type is used.
After stamping, attach plate to the adhesive-backed portion of [2].
ENLARGED SECTION A-A THRU TYPICAL STAMPED CHARACTER: .043 / .048
*FOR OTHER PLATE DETAILS SEE DSSM NO. 6.
Example plate shown: row A 194370S400001 / R; row B V09 .. TN, CAK0904W, 0; row C POR15, 113 13, columns numbered 1-30.
notes_internal: Item 1: third digit looks like 6 at 600 dpi, OCR read 3885853; marked uncertain.
Item 2: binder hole wipes out the middle digits; spacing fits three digits between '39' and '72' (count itself not certain).
Example plate row B: a hole punch hides characters after 'V09'.
Tag [A] on the folder is a reference to the shipping list, not an applied material.
Location rows C-18 and C-21..C-28 are blank in the table; rows with no data were skipped.
